site_name: Trumbull Data Center (80 Merritt Blvd; former Digital Realty HVN10, former Nasdaq data center)
operator: Aphorio Carter Critical Infrastructure Fund (AC Trumbull LLC); Digital Realty until Dec 2024
load_basis: Utility power capacity of the site (15 MW, 2N UPS) as stated at the Dec 2024 sale and repeated by CT Public/CT Mirror in Sept 2026. This is service capacity, an upper bound, not metered load or leased IT load; actual 2025 draw is not published and is likely well below 15 MW.
notes: 227,500 sq ft building on 8+ acres. Ownership chain per Westfair (2026-07-19): Nasdaq until 1996, Sentinel Properties 1996-2010, Digital Realty 2010-2024, AC Trumbull LLC (Aphorio Carter + CogNOVUM) from Dec 2024 for about $10M. No exact first-operation year found: the First Selectman says the property has been a data center 'since the 1960s' and CT Mirror says 'more than 50 years', so it predates 1976; energized_year left null rather than guessed. Utility: the only source naming UI is an EIA-derived listing for an on-site generator ('Digital Fairfield', EIA plant 62455) seen in a search snippet; the page itself returned 401 to a direct fetch, so this is unverified and marked low. Trumbull lies in UI's distribution territory. A proposed $200M AI-ready conversion (365 Data Centers / Aphorio Carter / CogNOVUM, 2026) is not operating; the applicant told the town it would not draw more than existing site capacity, and a Yale economist speculated a later request for 20-30 MW (not a filed plan). Matches the known OSM feature tagged Digital Realty New York HVN10.

site_name: CyrusOne NYM5 Norwalk (6 Norden Place; built for Cervalis)
serving_utility: Unconfirmed: operator says the site has power feeds from two utilities but does not name them; the site is in East Norwalk, where Norwalk Third Taxing District Electric and Eversource (CL&P) both operate
load_basis: Operator site page (fetched Nov 2026): '4 MW Total IT Capacity'. Built IT capacity, not metered load. CyrusOne's FY2021 10-K listed 'Norwalk I' at 6 MW critical load (gross UPS power installed), 17k colocation sq ft 100% occupied, 83k sq ft powered shell.
notes: Cervalis signed the 167,691 sq ft build-to-suit lease with Fortis Property Group in Aug 2012 (announced as 10 Norden Place); Westfair (2012-09-24) reported the design as 16 MW of utility power and 50,000 sq ft of raised floor. planned_full_buildout_mw = 16 is that utility-power design figure, not IT load. Opening year not confirmed from an allowed source: 2012 press projected 2013, a directory tracker says Feb 2014, and CyrusOne acquired Cervalis in July 2015, so first operation falls in 2013-2015; left null. FY2021 10-K source for the 6 MW figure: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1553023/000155302322000009/cone-20211231.htm. Directory listings citing 16 MW or 19 MW for this site conflict with the operator's own 4 MW IT figure and were not used. Third Taxing District search found no document naming this customer.

operator: CyrusOne (as of FY2021 10-K; 2025 status not confirmed)
load_basis: No 2025 figure found. CyrusOne FY2021 10-K: 5 MW critical load (gross UPS power installed), 20k colocation sq ft only 22% occupied, leasehold. Implied leased load at end-2021 was on the order of 1 MW.
notes: Under the 10 MW threshold; listed only because it is the third-largest sourced site in a state where EPRI's total is about 31 MW. Street address and coordinates not confirmed from an allowed source, so left null. It is NOT the known OSM feature 'amnet Data Center' (osm:way/878795698), which reverse-geocodes to Fahey Street in Springdale and is a separate small managed-services site (now Omega Systems). CyrusOne's current website no longer serves a Stamford page at the URLs tried, so the site may have been exited after 2021; unverified. Utility is a territory inference only (Stamford is in Eversource's CL&P territory), hence low.
